name: ink-sketch
title: Ink sketch
summary: Quirky big-eyed cartoon creatures in loose, hand-drawn pen and ink. Light: black ink on white paper. Dark: white highlight ink on charcoal paper, redrawn (never inverted). Both published as transparent ink-only pairs.

light: Create one original editorial illustration. Black ink on clean white paper, light mode.

REFERENCE ROLES: The FIRST reference is the house style anchor. Match its pen work, hatching density, creature design language, level of detail and humour exactly, but NOT its characters or its scene: never draw its explorer, its stage or its books unless the cast below asks for them. {castReference}The remaining references guide the drawing language only: the sheet of creatures shows the creature grammar (huge, slightly mismatched round eyes with dot pupils, very simple asymmetrical bodies, spindly limbs, expressive mouths, comically surprised or deadpan faces); the bird and cliff drawings guide energetic, imperfect, fast pen strokes with varied pressure, loose contours and expressive hatching. Never draw their bird, tree, cliff or exact animals.

VISUAL STORYTELLING: one clear, funny visual metaphor, legible at article width on a phone. Stage it through body language, expressions and props, never through labels. Everyone is an original quirky cartoon creature, never a realistic human, never stock-vector people, never smooth digital outlines or 3D rendering. No readable words, numbers, speech balloons, captions, logos, title, signature or watermark, unless the subject asks for a specific mark.

COMPOSITION: {format}. Keep every subject whole and uncropped, use roughly the middle 85 percent of the canvas, with generous untouched white paper around the drawing and only light grounding hatch marks below. No border, no frame, no dense backdrop filling the page.
INK: black ink only. Loose spontaneous hand-drawn pen lines, expressive hatching, irregular broken contours, comic editorial sketch. No colour, no grey wash, no gradients, no tone fills.
dark: Redraw the FIRST reference image, preserving its exact scene, layout{panels}, characters, poses, expressions, props, framing and placement, as a white-ink HIGHLIGHT sketch on opaque warm charcoal paper #191714. The SECOND reference is the approved dark-mode ink treatment: match it. The remaining references guide character style and expressive pen work only.

This is NOT an inversion, NOT a photographic negative, NOT white outlines traced from black contours. Draw LIGHT: white hatching selectively describes lit top and front planes, rim light, bright fur, faces, props and edges under an upper-left light. Bare dark paper carries the SHADOWS: dark undersides, crevices and shadow sides stay unmarked. Contours break and disappear in shade. Eyes stay expressive with dark pupils. Loose, energetic, imperfect white pen strokes, denser only at highlights. Never fill whole forms with solid white.
No grey airbrush, glow, colour, gradients, border, captions, signature or watermark. Keep any lettering the source has, and add none. Same size and composition as the source.
